newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Prince Philip angers anti-gun movement.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Prince Philip angers anti-gun movement.

text.p: Britain's Prince Philip angered anti-gun campaigners on Wednesday by saying that firearms enthusiasts were no more dangerous than golf players.
Queen Elizabeth's husband told a BBC radio interviewer that he believed that a new British law banning most handguns would not prevent future gun crimes.
The law was introduced after a misfit weapons enthusiast armed with pistols shot dead 16 schoolchildren and their teacher at a school in Dunblane, Scotland in March.
The killer, Thomas Hamilton, belonged to a gun club and had licences for the four weapons he used.
"I can't believe that the members of shooting clubs are any more dangerous than members of a squash club or a golf club or anything else," Prince Philip said.
"I don't see this sort of legislation preventing handguns getting into the hands of criminals," he added in the interview recorded for broadcast on Thursday but released in advance to the media.
The law passed in October gave Britain some of the toughest gun laws in the world, but it stopped short of banning .22 calibre handguns used for target shooting.
Prince Philip, like many members of the royal family, is a keen game hunter. He is also famed for often tactless remarks.
Ann Pearston, of the Snowdrop anti-gun group formed after the Dunblane killings, said he had caused deep offence.

"My reaction is absolute disbelief," Pearston told the BBC. "I think it will cause deep pain when the parents of the victims are getting through a very difficult time, their first Christmas (since the killings)."
The Snowdrop group is still campaigning for a ban on all handguns.
Earlier this month, animal rights groups were outraged when Prince Philip's grandson, Prince William, was reported to have shot his first deer.
